title: Latin, the Language That Lived On
objective: After this level you can explain how Latin spread and became the Romance languages.
summary: Latin spread west with soldiers and settlers, and spoken Latin became Italian, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Romanian.

cards.headline: The Western Empire fell. Its language kept going.
cards.body: Latin didn’t vanish with Rome. It grew up into languages people still speak.

cards.headline: From Latium to the West
cards.body: Latin started small, in Latium, the region around Rome. It was the language of the Latins, the first Romans. As Rome grew, Latin spread through the western provinces with soldiers, settlers and officials. The East was different: Greek stayed the common language there. Rome ruled the East, but the East kept talking Greek.

cards.headline: Latin’s children
cards.body: Everyday spoken Latin, often called Vulgar Latin, didn’t stay put. It gradually developed into the Romance languages, including Italian, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Romanian. English isn’t one of them, but a large share of its vocabulary comes from Latin, much of it through French. So even this sentence is partly Roman.

cards.fact: Latin outlived the empire that spread it.
cards.context: It remained the language of the Western Church, law and scholarship for centuries after the Western Empire fell. And Romanian descends from the Latin spoken along the lower Danube, including Dacia, the land Trajan conquered. Scholars still debate exactly where it first took shape.

cards.headline: Latin: still alive
learned: It spread across the western provinces
Spoken Latin became the Romance languages

questions.prompt: Which of these is a Romance language?

options.label: English
options.rationale: It borrowed Latin words but isn’t Romance.

options.label: Greek
options.rationale: It has its own ancient line.

questions.explanation: Portuguese is a Romance language, descended from spoken Latin.

questions.prompt: Why didn’t Latin replace Greek in the eastern provinces?

options.label: Rome banned Latin in the East
Greek was already the common language there
The East was never part of the empire
Latin had no written form yet

questions.explanation: Greek stayed the common language of the East, so Latin spread mainly in the West.

questions.prompt: From Level 58: Romanian grew from Latin spoken along the lower Danube, including which province Trajan conquered?

options.label: Britain
options.rationale: Its people later spoke other languages.

options.label: Egypt
options.rationale: Greek and Egyptian were spoken there.

questions.explanation: Romanian descends from the Latin of the lower Danube, including Dacia, roughly modern Romania; scholars debate exactly where it first took shape.
